key_insight: Evaluator bias in multi-agent LLM systems is contagious: even when agents share the same base model, biased judgments can propagate across the network at measurable levels.
engineering_relevance: For multi-agent AI systems, using larger evaluator committees and bias-aware evaluation design can materially reduce cross-agent contamination and improve reliability.
method: Defined Contagion Networks to model bias spread among interacting LLM agents.
Ran controlled 3-agent experiments with DeepSeek-chat under three evaluator profiles: structured, balanced, and evidence-based.
Measured the Cross-Agent Contagion Matrix (Gamma_3) and analyzed propagation regimes via the spectral radius rho(Gamma_N).
evidence_signal: In the 3-agent study, contagion coefficients ranged from 0.157 to 0.352, and increasing committee size from k=1 to k=3 reduced effective contagion by 72.4%.
watch_item: Results come from a controlled setup with one underlying model family, so transferability to larger, more diverse, or real-world agent networks may require further validation.
paper_title: Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
